text:
erin: Heads-up: after the kernel-selection bump yesterday we saw a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for web-search workload. Not sure if it's batching alignment or key normalization.
ben: ugh. saw something similar in staging traces. hot-prefix evictions spiked around the same deploy.
carla: can you paste the profiler snippet?
erin: copied from /prod/metrics/prefixcache/last24h: 
```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.66
kv_cache.evictions_per_min: 12 -> 56
avg_inflight_batch_size: 4.1 -> 2.2
kernel_selected: small-attn-v2
```
ben: avg batch size halved — that screams batching heuristic mismatch with the new kernel. new kernel has different optimal microbatch sizes and we might be falling back to smaller batches which changes prefix alignment (different token windows => different cache keys).
alice: are keys including tokenizer metadata? last month we started dropping tokenizer version by default for some routes to reduce key churn. could be related.
carla: good point. if the kernel reduces per-request seq_len via truncation or prepad we might be generating different tokenization boundaries.
erin: I grepped the logs: for many requests the tool/function-call fields remain identical but the probe shows additional whitespace normalization from preproc layer for the small-attn-v2 path. that would change the canonical key.
dave: quoting the keyer code: `make_prefix_key(prompt, tool_args, sys_prompt_meta, tokenizer_tag)` — tokenizer_tag sometimes empty. if kernel path sets `tokenizer_tag` to "auto" it will change key.
frank: quick mitigation: force tokenizer pin for affected routes to previous tag (v12pin) and set batching min to 4 on canary nodes. would that give immediate hit-rate improvement?
erin: canary applied — rolling patch: `redwoodctl patch nodepool canary --env=prod --set batching.min_inflight=4 --set tokenizer.tag=v12pin`
ops-bot: deploy started: canary pool (20 nodes) patch job 2245 initiated by erin.
ben: also saw an increase in KV cache serialization time after kernel switch. profile: `kv_serialize_ms p50: 1.2 -> 3.8` maybe due to different key lengths (more metadata serialized).
carla: we should audit what metadata small-attn-v2 path injects. my hunch: it appends `kernel_hint` + `microbatch_id` into keymeta for debugging, which previously only lived in logs and accidentally got folded into key struct.
alice: if that's the case we have both a correctness and cost problem: unnecessary key variance and bigger serialized keys -> higher mem + GC churn. revert asap.
erin: timeline proposal: 1) rollback keymeta injection on kernel path (hotfix) 2) pin tokenizer on canary (already applied) 3) run A/B: kernel-selection v2 with old keyer vs v2 with fixed keyer 4) longer term: add unit test that checks key stability across kernel selection permutations.
frank: add a perf test that simulates 30k short-prefix queries with varied toolfields to baseline hit-rate delta. I can add to perfbench.
dave: also flag for ops: eviction surge increased OOM risk on a few pods. ops: please monitor `kv_mem_pressure` alarms.
ops-bot: alarm set: kv_mem_pressure > 0.85 for 3m. notify #eng-oncall.
ben: one more observation — batching heuristic decreased average seq_len observed by the runtime because microbatch alignment shifts tokenization boundaries; even with the same text, if we truncate to fit new kernel's max_chunk we end up with different keys. so even normalizing whitespace won't fully restore hits unless tokenizer and chunking logic are consistent.
carla: sounds like we need a canonicalization contract: canonicalized_prompt = normalize_whitespace(normalize_json_args(tool_args)) + tokenizer_tag + stable_sys_prompt_id. then kernel selection must not mutate canonicalization fields or otherwise we should normalize after kernel decisions (but before keying).
erin: agreed. I'll open a PR for keyer changes and a follow-up to runtime: ensure kernel hints don't flow into keymeta.
alice: +1. also add an integration test that runs both kernels against same input and asserts identical keys for identical logical request (modulo allowed tags).
frank: I'll schedule the perfbench run after hotfix. timeline: hotfix in next 30m, measure 1h, then A/B for 24h.
erin: thanks. if canary hit-rate recovers we can promote. keeping an eye on latency SLOs too — small-attn-v2 improved tail latency, don't want to throw that away if fix is simple.
ben: noted. collect per-route hit-rate and per-kernel batch distribution so we can correlate. I'll dump a CSV and post.
erin: posted the CSV to thread: https://internal/redwood/reports/prefixcache-correlation-1723456789.csv
carla: thanks. looping in eng-ml to validate kernel heuristics later today.
erin: tagging @carla @ben @alice @dave for follow-ups. will update when canary completes.
